catalog_quote: San Maka is a tonal language with three level tones, designated, according to the IPA, by diacritics: acute (high), macron (mid) and grave (low). Vowel sequences may bear the following combinations of tones: level cv́v́; cv̄v̄; cv̀v̀ / falling cv́v̀; cv́v̄; cv̄v̀ / rising cv̀v́; cv̄v́ / Susanne Platiel focused on distribution of tonal units according to the types of syllables and words. She showed that words of the CVCV structure cannot carry the mid tone in both syllables if they contain closed or semi-closed vowels: /i/, /u/, /e/, /o/ (Platiel 1974: 132). Platiel also pointed out the rarity of tonal minimal pairs and triplets: it is difficult to find three or four identical segment chains that would differ only by tone

new_statements.rule_in_words: San Maka (Southern Samo) is a three-level tone language (H, M, L, plus contour combinations on vowel sequences); tone is lexically and grammatically distinctive. Neither of the two accessible modern descriptions (Perekhvalskaya 2017, 2021) mentions word stress, accent or metrical prominence at all; no statement about where stress falls exists in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress (source is silent). Tonal restriction noted: CVCV words with close/half-close vowels cannot be M-M (Platiel 1974: 132).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone description; citation forms of nouns and verbs (neutral form is the dictionary form). Nothing on phrase-level prominence or intonation.
new_statements.identity_note: Perekhvalskaya's 'San Maka' / 'Southern San (san-maka)' is the southern variety of the San/Samo cluster (Toma area, Nayala province), the same variety as Platiel's 'parler samo de Toma' and Ki's 'san du sud ou parler de Toma'; Glottolog files all of these under sout2844 Southern Samo [sbd]. Northern varieties (Matya stj, Maya sym) are separate languages with low mutual intelligibility. Glottolog's Daniel & Shaw 1977 'Samo phonemes' is Papua New Guinea Samo, misassigned.

tone_statements.citation: Perekhvalskaya, Elena. 2021. Grammatical functions of tone in San Maka. Mandenkan 65: 333-348. doi:10.4000/mandenkan.2574 (Section 2.1.5 Tonal system)
tone_statements.quote: San Maka is a tonal language with three level tones, designated, according to the IPA, by diacritics: acute (high), macron (mid) and grave (low). Vowel sequences may bear the following combinations of tones: level cv́ v́ ; cv̄ v̄ ; cv̀ v̀ falling cv́ v̀ ; cv́ v̄ ; cv̄ v̀ rising cv̀ v́ ; cv̄ v́ … Platiel also pointed out the rarity of tonal minimal pairs and triplets: it is difficult to find three or four identical segment chains that would differ only by tone (Platiel 1974: 144).
tone_statements.locator: pp. 336-337, section 2.1.5 'Tonal system'; grammatical tone in section 3, pp. 339-345
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (high, mid, low); falling and rising patterns are sequences of level tones on two vowels; rich grammatical tone (perfective M(L) melody, tone raising in compounds, tonal allomorphs).

tone_statements.citation: Platiel, Suzy [Suzanne]. 1990. Les sous-catégories du procès en san: diathèse et composition. Mandenkan 19: 69-81.
tone_statements.quote: Remarque: On notera que dans presque tous les exemples cités présentant deux noms se suivant immédiatement, le second subit un relèvement tonal par rapport à son ton de base : “le nom” ----> tɔ à ton moyen qui prend un ton haut dans pérä-tɔ Ce changement de ton est conforme à la règle qui s'applique dans tous les cas de syntagmes nominaux servant à exprimer une caractérisation .
tone_statements.translation: Note: in almost all the examples cited with two nouns in immediate succession, the second undergoes a tonal raising relative to its basic tone: 'the name' -> tɔ with mid tone, which takes a high tone in pérä-tɔ. This change of tone conforms to the rule that applies in all cases of noun phrases expressing a characterisation.
tone_statements.locator: p. 84 (under the page number '- 84 -'), 'Remarque' closing the section on composition, before 'La composition systématique';: 'reléve-\nment' dehyphenated and accent normalised to 'relèvement'
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Three registers (bas, moyen, haut) referred to; contour ('mélodique') tones arise on monosyllables under reduplication; grammatical/derivational tone: H-toned diminutive suffix, M-toned suffix, tone raising of the second noun in noun+noun (characterisation) phrases, one-register lowering of unpossessed body-part nouns and of readers=patient verb forms.

tone_statements.translation: the omission of the second participant is marked by a change of tone on the verb, which expresses amalgamation with the 3rd person singular personal pronoun /à/; thus one has [...] 'this woman made the pot fall' [...] but, with a change of tone on 'fall': [...] 'the pot fell'

tone_statements.citation: Platiel, Suzy [Suzanne]. 1981. La formation des verbes en san. Mandenkan 2: 69-83.
tone_statements.quote: Le systéme tonal du san admet les trois tons ponctuels suivants : bas (B), moyen (M), et haut (H). L’étude du syst@me tonal en san (cf. Ki 1985) montre que les unités lexicales connaissent les schémes tonals suivants : B, M, H, BB, BH, HB, HH, MM!. Ainsi, si nous optons pour l’interprétation V,V, de la longueur vocalique, les successions … de tons possibles sont : HH, HB, BH, BB, MM. Ce qui signifie que chacune des voyelles de la suite V,V, porte un ton.
tone_statements.translation: The tonal system of San admits the following three level (punctual) tones: low (B), mid (M), and high (H). The study of the tonal system in San (cf. Ki 1985) shows that lexical units have the following tone patterns: B, M, H, BB, BH, HB, HH, MM [fn. 1]. Thus, if we opt for the V1V2 interpretation of vowel length, the possible tone sequences are: HH, HB, BH, BB, MM. Which means that each of the vowels of the V1V2 sequence bears a tone.
tone_statements.locator: p. 4-5, section 2.1 'Argument lié au système tonal' (with fn. 1 on p. 4)
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones, low, mid and high; each vowel (both halves of V1V2) bears a tone, so falling/rising are HB/BH sequences; head-noun tone raised one register after a determiner; low-tone perfective.

sources.note: A syntactic-semantic account of how San builds verb concepts from a small stock of verb radicals plus nominal participants. Tone enters once: verbs are cited in three aspectual forms (acc., inac., zero, e.g. bɔ-bée-bɔ 'enlever', footnote 2) and, for two-participant verbs, omission of the second participant 'est marquée par un changement de ton du procès' (amalgam with the 3sg pronoun à), illustrated with 'faire tomber' vs 'tomber'. No tone inventory or tone rules beyond this.

sources.citation: Platiel, Suzanne. 1994. La nasalité en san. Linguistique africaine 13: 131-176.
sources.note: Article on the vowel system: San words carry tone marks and the tone of a lost final vowel is said to survive on the final nasal, but no tone inventory or rule is given; nothing on word stress.

tone.quote: CVN : disparition de 1a vo; d elle (et peut-étre de la syllabe finale) dont le ton, cependant, a ete conservé et se réalise sur N quand ii est différent de v. … puisqu'a I'exception des voyelles /e/ et /o/ qui n'existent pas dans le systéme des voyelles nasales et sont admises devant N, toutes les autres voyelles, de méme que les combinaisons tona-les se retrouvent aussi bien dans les successions CYY que CVN.
tone.locator: p. 262, 'Création d'une voyelle nasale', schema of the three syllabic formulas (CVN branch) and the paragraph after it
tone.translation: CVN: loss of the [final] vowel (and perhaps of the final syllable), whose tone, however, has been preserved and is realised on N when it is different from [that of] V. … since, apart from the vowels /e/ and /o/, which do not exist in the nasal-vowel system and are admitted before N, all the other vowels, as well as the tonal combinations, are found in CVV sequences as well as in CVN. (scanned text: '1a vo; d elle' = 'la voyelle', 'ii' = 'il', 'CYY' = 'CVV'.)
